title: Arithmetic series
examples: What is the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series?
How do I find the number of terms if I know the sum?
Can you show an example of finding the nth term from the end?

explain.say: Today we learn about arithmetic series. These are sequences with a constant difference. We will learn to find the nth term and the sum.
The nth term formula is a equals b plus negative one times n. Here, a is the nth term, b is the first term, and n is the term number.
Let us find the fifth term of a sequence starting with two, four, six. The common difference is two. So the fifth term is two plus four times two, which equals ten.
The sum formula for the first n terms is n divided by two times the sum of the first and last term. This is the formula S<0xE2><0x82><0x99> equals n divided by two times (b plus a<0xE2><0x82><0x99>).
To find the nth term from the end, we use a similar idea. If there are n terms total, the nth term from the end is simply the first term plus the common difference times negative n plus one.

faq.q: What is the common difference in an arithmetic series?
faq.a: It is the constant number you add to get from one term to the next. You find it by subtracting any term from the term that follows it.
asks: How do I find the difference?

faq.q: When should I use the sum formula S<0xE2><0x82><0x99>?
faq.a: You use this formula when you need to find the total when you add up a certain number of terms. Remember you need to know the number of terms first.
asks: How do I find the total sum?
Is there a formula for adding them up?

faq.q: Does the nth term formula work for any sequence?
faq.a: No, the nth term formula only works for arithmetic sequences. These sequences must have a constant difference between terms.
asks: Can I use this for squares?
Does it only work for straight lines?

faq.q: How do I find the number of terms if I know the sum?
faq.a: You usually need more information, like the last term or the common difference. You might have to set up an equation using the sum formula.
asks: What if I know the sum but not the number of terms?
Can I work backwards from the sum?

faq.q: What does 'nth term from the end' actually mean?
faq.a: It means finding the value of a term counting backwards from the very last term. If there are twenty terms, the first term from the end is the twentieth term.
asks: How do I count from the back?
What is the last term from the end?

facts: An arithmetic series has a constant difference between consecutive terms.
The formula for the nth term is a subscript n equals b plus (n minus one) times d.
The sum of the first n terms is S subscript n equals n divided by two times (b plus a subscript n).
The common difference, d, is found by subtracting any term from the next term.

quiz.say: Find the sum of the first ten terms of 5, 10, 15, ...
quiz.why: The first term is five, the common difference is five, and there are ten terms. The sum is ten divided by two times (five plus ninety-five), which equals two hundred seventy-five.

wrong.0: This answer incorrectly assumes the sum is just the number of terms times the common difference.
wrong.1: This answer incorrectly adds the first and last term and multiplies by ten instead of using the correct sum formula.
wrong.3: This answer incorrectly calculates the last term as ninety instead of ninety-five.

quiz.say: In a sequence with a first term of 50 and a common difference of negative three, what is the fifth term from the end if there are fifteen terms total?
quiz.why: The fifth term from the end is the thirteenth term. Using the formula, it is fifty plus (thirteen minus one) times negative three, which equals twenty.

wrong.0: This answer incorrectly calculates the term number as five instead of fifteen minus four.
wrong.1: This answer incorrectly uses the common difference as positive when it should be negative.
wrong.3: This answer incorrectly assumes the term from the end is always the first term.
